## Which factor is negative?

A negative product requires opposite signs. A target sum of $1$ or $-1$ means the absolute values are one apart.

:::::: {.example-pair}

::::: {.model}

<h3>Worked example</h3>

$x^2+x-12$

::: {.fragment}

**P** $=-12$, **S** $=1$. Give the number farther from zero the positive sign.

:::

::: {.fragment}

| Signed pair | Sum |
|:--|:--|
| $-1,\ 12$ | $11$ |
| $-2,\ 6$ | $4$ |
| $-3,\ 4$ | $1$ |

:::

::: {.fragment}

**F:** Select $-3,4$: $-3+4=1$.

:::

::: {.fragment}

$x^2+x-12=(x-3)(x+4)$

:::

:::::

::::: {.paper}

::: {.fragment}

<h3>Your turn</h3>

$x^2-x-12$

Which factors of 12 are one apart? List the signed pairs, choose and check.

:::

::: {.fragment}

**P** $=-12$, **S** $=-1$. Give the number farther from zero the negative sign.

:::

::: {.fragment}

| Signed pair | Sum |
|:--|:--|
| $1,\ -12$ | $-11$ |
| $2,\ -6$ | $-4$ |
| $3,\ -4$ | $-1$ |

:::

::: {.fragment}

**F:** Select $3,-4$: $3-4=-1$.

:::

::: {.fragment}

$(x+3)(x-4)=x^2-4x+3x-12$

$=x^2-x-12$

:::
